mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances with declining RSAFS, or the correlation between RSAFS decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which increases corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decrease and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% each within two months signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 2% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between HOUST and RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a deflationary pressure, which increases real purchasing power but also indicates a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL decrease and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% each within two months signals a strengthening economy, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 0.5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between INDPRO increase and UNRATE decrease and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
